subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex WebSocket and Unix opening handshakes use the proposed fixed 30-second fail-closed bound and revised error/exit event contract?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but the timeout changes previously unbounded behavior and the event-forwarding rule is a transport-contract choice that automated checks cannot settle.

options.title: Accept the 30-second contract
options.body: Merge the fixed private timeout and use `error` when subscribed plus `exit` as the universal stalled-handshake signal.

options.title: Select another shared duration
options.body: Keep the transport-level fix but have the Codex owner choose a different established connection-policy duration before merge.

options.title: Retain unbounded handshakes
options.body: Reject the fail-closed change and continue allowing incomplete upgrades to hold initialize and RPC calls indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second contract
recommendation.body: Merge the fixed private timeout and use `error` when subscribed plus `exit` as the universal stalled-handshake signal.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available repository-level decision owner, though direct Codex-area history routing could not be established in this sandbox.
